title: Redwood Dedicated capacity discovery - Seabreeze Financial
next_steps: Send Dedicated pricing and commitment tiers
Schedule SE-led benchmark/demo in Redwood Dedicated environment w/ sample workload
Provide sizing estimate for reserved GPUs and burst policy options
action_items: Maya Chen: Send pricing + sample contract (due: 2026-03-06)
Daniel Ortiz: Run follow-up benchmark plan and propose GPU sizing (due: 2026-03-10)
Sofia Martinez: Share current traffic patterns and peak qps by model (due: 2026-03-06)
summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) for Seabreeze's conversational AI and extraction workloads. Main concerns: data isolation, predictable latency, burst scaling, autoscaling policies, and security/compliance (SOC 2, SSO, KMS). SE to propose sizing & benchmark plan; AE to share pricing and security pack.
topics: current stack and pain points; throughput/latency SLOs; reserved GPU sizing; burst and autoscale strategies; networking/VPC and KMS; observability and rollout strategy; procurement timeline and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, along with Daniel, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Harpreet Singh: Good, thanks. Excited to get into this — we've been looking at dedicated options.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Yeah hi, Liam here. We're evaluating a move off our hosted experimentation to reserved capacity for production. Main drivers are latency consistency and data isolation.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great, that's exactly what Dedicated is for. Quick intros? Daniel, want to say hi.
[00:24] Daniel Ortiz: Hey all, Daniel — I focus on infra/benchmarks and will dig into sizing and burst behaviour in a bit.
[00:30] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, infra lead. We'll own the VPC setup and connectivity. A few red flags for us: we need KMS integration, strict audit logs, SSO, and the ability to restrict model telemetry.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally — we have KMS/HSM integrations for Private but Dedicated supports customer-managed keys too; we'll share the docs.
[00:46] Liam O'Connor: Cool. For context, our workload is a mix: real-time chat (low latency, sub-120ms token time desirable), and nightly batch extraction for ledger processing where throughput matters more. We're using a small ensemble of 2 models — a 7B-ish instruction model for chat and a 13B extraction model.
[01:04] Daniel Ortiz: Helpful. Do you have qps numbers and typical sequence lengths?
[01:08] Liam O'Connor: Baseline is 40 qps steady for chat, with spikes to 400 qps during morning runs for 5-7 minutes. Batch job runs overnight ~200k tokens per hour. Typical chat context ~800 tokens, extraction runs up to 2k.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Okay that spike-to-steady ratio is common. Dedicated can do reserved pools plus burst to shared capacity or pre-warmed burst nodes depending on commit. We should talk about burst strategy and autoscaling windows.
[01:34] Harpreet Singh: Burst to shared capacity worries us because of data isolation. We can't have sensitive requests go to multi-tenant hosts.
[01:40] Daniel Ortiz: Understood. We can configure Dedicated so burst only uses other reserved pools in your tenant or isolated 'burst' group that you control — or we can approve a hard cap and recommend slight overcommit in reserved GPUs. There's also a model variant route: lower-cost quantized variants for background jobs.
[01:56] Sofia Martinez: Can you explain the mechanism? Is burst spinning up new VMs or routing to other hardware? How quick is it?
[02:02] Daniel Ortiz: It depends on the policy. Two options: 1) Warm standby instances that allow sub-minute scale up, or 2) elastic burst that routes to compatible hosted variants — which is faster but multi-tenant. For strict isolation you choose warm standby or pre-provision extra reserved GPUs for headroom.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: What about autoscale granularity? We need per-model scaling not per-tenant because the 13B extraction job can't impact chat model latency.
[02:28] Daniel Ortiz: Right — Redwood's routing is per-model and per-route. You can pin models to specific GPU pools and set separate autoscale policies per pool. Also can set priority-based routing so chat routes have higher latency SLOs.
[02:40] Harpreet Singh: Any evictions or warm-start cache issues? We rely heavily on KV cache for chat long contexts — cold starts kill us.
[02:48] Daniel Ortiz: KV cache is supported; the runtime manages KV cache populations across requests. For Dedicated we persist cache on the serving instance and we suggest sticky routing to keep session locality. For burst to standby, there is cache warming time; we can do prefetch strategies for expected sessions.
[03:02] Sofia Martinez: Encryption at rest — can we use our KMS?
[03:05] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS keys for model and token cache encryption. We'll include the integration guide.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: Latency SLO — you mentioned sub-120ms target. Is that end-to-end or token generation?
[03:16] Daniel Ortiz: That would be per-token generation tail latency on dedicated GPUs for the chat model. End-to-end including network will be a bit higher; with regional placement and minimized hops you should see under 200ms for typical messages.
[03:28] Harpreet Singh: What's the recommended GPU type and count? We're leaning to A100s or H100s.
[03:34] Daniel Ortiz: For 13B extraction at 2k seq, H100s give better throughput, but A100s can work with higher concurrency. Initial guess: for 40 steady qps and 400 qps spikes, a small pool of 4-6 H100-equivalents for chat plus 2-4 for batch/extraction depending on quantization. We'll run a sizing benchmark to refine.
[03:54] Maya Chen: We'll follow up with a concrete sizing proposal after we see your real traffic patterns.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: How does pricing for Dedicated look vs hosted? We have procurement noise around minimum commitments.
[04:04] Maya Chen: Dedicated is commit-based. Monthly reserved capacity pricing, plus an optional burst overlay. We'll send tiered pricing showing monthly vs annual discounts and recommended minimums aligned with the sizing.
[04:14] Harpreet Singh: Security/compliance — SOC 2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. Can you cover those?
[04:21] Maya Chen: Yes. Redwood Dedicated customers get audit logs, RBAC integrated with SSO (SAML/OIDC), and we can provide SOC 2 and ISO artifacts. For Private installs we offer air-gapped options; for Dedicated we still have strict tenancy and logs. We'll attach the security pack to the follow-up email.
[04:34] Sofia Martinez: How do model updates/rollouts work? We need canaries and rollback and to smoke test quality.
[04:39] Daniel Ortiz: There's rollout tooling — canary, A/B, automatic rollback on regression alarms. We can tie quality checks to your evals and block rollouts if metrics degrade.
[04:47] Liam O'Connor: Any limits on custom model uploads? We may want to bring our fine-tuned checkpoints.
[04:52] Daniel Ortiz: You can upload models; we support model versioning and pinning. For very custom ops we may need to validate but generally supported.
[04:58] Harpreet Singh: Networking — we need VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allow lists.
[05:03] Maya Chen: Supported. We'll share VPC onboarding docs. For Dedicated we can do PrivateLink-like endpoints and peering.
[05:10] Sofia Martinez: Observability — token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards?
[05:14] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Console gives per-route token cost, per-model tail latency, traces, and ingestion of traces to your existing observability stack.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: Timeframe — procurement wants to close pilot within 4 weeks if we like results. Is that realistic?
[05:28] Maya Chen: Yes — we can do a 2-4 week pilot. SE-led benchmark in your Dedicated sandbox within a week of getting access and traffic samples.
[05:35] Harpreet Singh: Anything in the contract about data retention and logs? We need to keep logs for at least 1 year.
[05:40] Maya Chen: We have configurable log retention tiers; we'll include options.
[05:44] Liam O'Connor: Okay, can we summarize next steps?
[05:47] Maya Chen: Sure. We'll: 1) Send pricing and contract template; 2) Share SOC2/security docs & VPC onboarding; 3) Daniel will propose a benchmark plan and sizing; 4) Seabreeze to share traffic patterns and sample payloads.
[05:59] Sofia Martinez: I'll send traffic patterns and recent perf traces.
[06:02] Liam O'Connor: Thanks — excited to see the sizing.
[06:05] Maya Chen: Great — we'll follow up with dates for the benchmark. Appreciate your time.
[06:09] Harpreet Singh: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript contains some minor transcription errors (names occasionally mis-transcribed), some timestamps approximate.
